newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG might drop mercenary plan - PM Chan.
newsitem.headline: PNG might drop mercenary plan - PM Chan.

text.p: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan said on Wednesday his government would consider dropping a plan to use foreign mercenaries to help quash a rebellion on Bougainville island.

Chan told a news conference after a day of rising tension in the South Pacific nation that international and domestic opposition to the plan might make it unworkable and his cabinet would discuss calling it off.
Chan last month agreed a contract with the British company Sandline International for foreign mercenaries to train PNG troops and help them end the nine-year secessionist uprising.
The plan has drawn international criticism and on Monday Chan was forced to sack army commander Jerry Singirok after Singirok demanded Chan quit over the mercenary plan.
"The security aspects of the engagement...have been compromised by the publicity," Chan said. "The enemy are probably more prepared than us."

Chan said six of 40 Sandline mercenaries left Papua New Guinea on Wednesday, but the bulk of them were still being kept in barracks by the army. He said the army's new acting commander had complete control of the defence force.
